districts.reasoning: Cowpea-belt and Coastal Deeh livelihoods combine fragile crop income with livestock and purchased staples. Persistent rural delivery barriers motivate lower p and higher gamma as access-based judgments, without assuming rapid fatal exits. Rainfall-driven production, seasonal milk availability and interruptions to trade motivate elevated omega.

Shabelle irrigation, farming and proximity to Mogadishu diversify food sources, while longstanding displacement settlements add household vulnerability. The urban corridor motivates moderately higher p, but unequal food and service access keeps gamma elevated. Flood exposure, agricultural seasons and recurrent population movements motivate higher omega.

Cattle pastoralism and livestock trade coexist with persistent displacement hosting and uneven rural services. Dependence on livestock purchasing power motivates higher gamma, while variable reach beyond serviced settlements limits the elicited p. Rainfall-sensitive grazing, border trade interruptions and displacement movements motivate elevated omega.

Juba pump irrigation, sorghum farming and pastoral livelihoods coexist with displacement hosting and restricted roads. This mix motivates elevated gamma and a middle-range p that allows for town services alongside rural delivery barriers. River fluctuations, harvest timing, livestock conditions and transport disruption motivate higher omega.

Southern cattle and rainfed livelihoods offer several food sources, but insecure routes constrain their reliability. Rural delivery barriers motivate lower p, while persistent livelihood and market constraints motivate moderately elevated gamma. Seasonal pasture and crop changes, coastal trading conditions and conflict-related interruptions motivate elevated omega.

West Golis pastoralism and northwest farming provide complementary food and income pathways. This diversification motivates lower gamma, while rural travel requirements keep p below the major urban service centres. Gu-Karan rainfall, crop timing and seasonal water costs motivate moderate omega.

The district combines Shabelle farming with cowpea-belt and coastal livelihoods and a trade link to Mogadishu. Production potential moderates gamma, but insecure routes and unequal rural service access limit p. Flooding in riverine areas, agricultural labour cycles and repeated transport interruptions motivate elevated omega.

Mogadishu offers diverse markets and referral services alongside persistent displaced settlements and insecure household income. Urban service concentration motivates higher p, while displacement-related deprivation offsets some of the downward pressure on gamma from diversified livelihoods. Changing arrivals, evictions, casual employment and food prices motivate appreciable omega despite urban supply buffers.

Coastal Deeh fishing and pastoral livelihoods provide complementary earnings but depend on purchased staples and distant supply routes. Diversification moderates gamma, while remoteness motivates a restrained p. Fishing seasons, rough-sea trading conditions, rainfall-sensitive livestock income and transport costs motivate moderate omega.

Coastal trade and fishing complement surrounding rainfed and irrigated farming. Multiple food pathways moderate gamma, while insecure movement between settlements limits the service advantage assumed for p. Crop seasons, coastal conditions and recurring road interruptions motivate moderately elevated omega.

The district combines a sorghum-producing hinterland with a major, persistent displacement destination. Concentrated town services motivate higher p, while displaced households' limited assets and insecure rural livelihoods motivate higher gamma. Harvest and labour cycles, rainfall variability and repeated arrivals motivate high omega.

Shabelle riverine production and pastoral trade coexist with displacement and flood-exposed settlements. Town referral access motivates a moderate p, while recurrent livelihood losses and unequal food access motivate higher gamma. Flood pulses, cultivation cycles and associated population movement motivate a particularly elevated omega.

Border commerce and pastoral livelihoods coexist with established displacement hosting. Trade opportunities moderate gamma, but household asset loss and uneven service reach prevent a low-incidence assessment or a strongly elevated p. Border interruptions, livestock seasons and changing population movements motivate elevated omega.

Port commerce and urban employment broaden food access, while the rural district includes Guban and West Golis livelihoods. The urban market and service base motivate higher p and comparatively lower gamma, allowing for poorer rural households. Import prices, port employment and pastoral seasonality motivate a modest omega rather than assuming uniformly stable conditions.

Urban trade and northwest crop-livestock livelihoods provide diverse food pathways, alongside established displaced communities. Relative service accessibility motivates higher p, while livelihood diversification motivates lower gamma with a displacement allowance. Crop seasons, water costs and household earnings motivate a comparatively modest omega.

Port employment and trade coexist with displaced settlements and a pastoral hinterland. Urban referral opportunities motivate higher p, but market-dependent poor and displaced households keep gamma above diversified highland centres. Shipping seasons, casual labour, imported food prices and changing arrivals motivate moderate omega.

Juba irrigation and adjacent agropastoral and cattle livelihoods have productive potential but face persistent insecurity and delivery barriers. Constrained recovery pathways motivate lower p, while livelihood exclusion and unreliable access to food motivate higher gamma. River fluctuations, crop seasons and disruptions to trade and assistance motivate high omega.

Riverine cultivation and inland pastoral livelihoods depend on routes affected by longstanding encirclement of the town. Restricted delivery motivates lower p, and fragile purchasing power motivates elevated gamma despite local production. River conditions, harvest cycles and repeated changes in commodity access motivate high omega.

Town service concentration motivates higher p, while rural market dependence and vulnerable urban households motivate intermediate gamma. This dependence motivates intermediate gamma, while easier access around the town only partly raises p for the wider district. Gu-Deyr pasture cycles, water purchases and livestock-to-cereal prices motivate moderate omega.

_metadata.status: Subjective, context-informed high-concentration elicitation; not empirically calibrated parameter estimates.

interpretation.p: Monthly probability of any exit from the modeled state, including recovery, death and the model's loss-to-follow-up definition; not a treatment success probability.
interpretation.gamma: Mean monthly new entrants divided by the district under-5 population; fraction per month, not percentage or annual rate.
interpretation.omega: Total standard deviation of monthly new entrants divided by the district under-5 population; not a standard error or additional overdispersion component.
interpretation.population_scale: For under-5 population N, monthly arrival mean is gamma*N and monthly arrival standard deviation is omega*N.
interpretation.time_invariance: Each parameter describes a single district background environment across 2017-2021; recurring seasons and shocks inform the incidence-process variability, not year-specific parameter values.

elicitation_method.numerical_anchors: Analyst-chosen monthly means: p 0.22-0.39, gamma 0.0055-0.0140 and omega 0.0025-0.0065. These numerical scales are assumptions, not measurements supplied by the sources.
elicitation_method.mechanism: Livelihood diversity, asset dependence, displacement and reliable food access determine the gamma ordering; expected delivery and referral access determine the p ordering; recurring production, rainfall, river, market and movement changes determine the omega ordering.
elicitation_method.concentration_assignment: Better refers to relatively stronger contextual triangulation, standard to livelihood and regional contextual evidence, and limited to greater district-specific inference. These are analyst judgments, not validated evidence-quality scores or effective numbers of observed children.
elicitation_method.uncertainty_rule: Weaker district evidence reduces concentration, especially for omega; missing evidence never increases the omega mean.
elicitation_method.joint_prior: The requested marginal Beta distributions are supplied; no dependence between p, gamma and omega has been elicited.
elicitation_method.district_aggregation: Districts can span several livelihood zones and urban, rural and displaced populations. The district judgments acknowledge these mixtures but are not computed from unavailable district under-5 subgroup weights.

evidence_limits.outcome_separation: Only separable livelihood, market, climate, displacement, health-system and access context informed the priors; nutritional outcome content encountered incidentally in mixed search results was discarded. No nutritional prevalence, outcome-derived classification, estimated treatment burden or nutritional outcome ranking was used for calibration.
evidence_limits.ipc_acute_food_insecurity_baseline: A clean district-by-district multi-year sequence was not established. No district is assigned an asserted typical IPC Acute Food Insecurity phase; livelihood and food-access mechanisms are used instead.
evidence_limits.cmam_and_health_services: No verified 2017-2021 district CMAM coverage series, reliable supply-chain performance series or complete district health-density dataset was obtained. Town-service advantages and rural delivery penalties in p are explicitly hypotheses; facility presence alone does not establish treatment coverage.
evidence_limits.mortality_and_duration: Context does not identify whether exits are predominantly recovery or death, or establish an acute-and-fatal versus chronic-and-persistent district phenotype. No district-specific mortality uplift or spontaneous-recovery advantage was asserted; lower p represents an access-based duration hypothesis, not measured natural history.
evidence_limits.displacement: Historical hosting and repeated movement are distinguished where records support them. Flow monitoring does not by itself measure district displacement stock, and district hosting evidence was not available equally across all 74 districts.
evidence_limits.temporal_scope: Later security changes and post-2021 displacement or health-system conditions were not transported into the target-period district assessments. Individual bad seasons were used only as evidence of recurring mechanisms, not as the typical district mean.
evidence_limits.informativeness: High concentration is imposed to meet the requested prior strength. Contextual documents support qualitative mechanisms more strongly than precise numerical rates; concentration is not a claim of empirically demonstrated confidence and these priors warrant sensitivity analysis before operational use.

source_access_and_alternatives.status: Tools landing page inaccessible. Baseline index, joint 2015 livelihood map and 2016 consolidated profiles accessible; several individual baseline PDFs also accessible. The standalone West Golis PDF repeatedly timed out, so its structural information was taken from the consolidated profiles. Other standalone baseline links that failed were likewise replaced by the consolidated source.

source_access_and_alternatives.requested_source: FEWS NET Somalia map and profiles
source_access_and_alternatives.status: Country page and 2015 map pages returned HTTP 403. The coauthored FSNAU-FEWS NET map and livelihood profiles were read from FSNAU instead.

Publication index accessible. Mixed technical-release material was not used where outcome context could not be safely separated; outcome-free market and climate updates provided the multi-year contextual checks instead.

source_access_and_alternatives.requested_source: WHO/UNICEF health-system and CMAM coverage assessments
source_access_and_alternatives.status: SARA 2016 catalog and study description accessible; the catalog PDF download failed, ministry copies were blocked or exceeded the browser size limit. Catalog information and the accessible Garowe baseline health-service section were used; no district CMAM coverage percentages or mortality rates were invented.
OCHA landing page returned HTTP 403. OCHA's 2020 access overview was read through its ecoi.net mirror; FSNAU market reporting supplied additional evidence of repeatedly besieged supply routes.

UNHCR August 2019 PRMN document and an IOM Gedo report page were accessible; some IOM PDFs and other dashboard downloads returned HTTP 403 or cache errors. Historical IOM indexed report text and movement-report archives supplied the additional hosting and flow evidence; these were not treated as complete district censuses.
